runtimeRequirements: Pi interactive UI for select/input/editor/custom prompts

single-question TUI calls share the Locus session-generation inline interaction queue and keep Other/text editing inside the same non-overlay component; RPC uses native select/input requests, while multi-select/default/timeout orchestration remains ask-owned
Custom and fallback selectors are presented as typed SELECT surfaces; free-text follow-ups are typed INPUT surfaces
Official Pi dialog results use string or undefined; a known legacy object result is normalized by the local adapter
Interactive cancellation records a cancelled decision, while no-UI modes fail unavailable without recording a fake user decision

the shared inline interaction slot fences Pi's own close callback by slot ownership: a component the host silently replaced can no longer run the host's editor-restore path, so a late timeout, abort, or queued key from a superseded prompt cannot blank the interaction that replaced it, and the incumbent is retired only once the newcomer's factory has produced a component, so a request that never appears cannot take the slot; when a factory rejects, Pi restores the editor over the live component anyway, so the incumbent is explicitly retired on that path too and its owner is told rather than left awaiting a surface that is off the screen; a retired caller sees the typed stale error and reports benign replacement rather than failure — the ask tool reports it as status superseded with a retryable message instead of Ask UI failed
